R134.note: Hosting PowerShell in-process and passing serverName via AddParameter closes the injection, but the response silently changes from powershell.exe's formatted stdout to r.ToString() of PSObjects (type names, not the ping table), all exceptions are newly mapped to 400, and a heavy Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK dependency is added - none of it stated.

R135.note: BASE_DIR.resolve then toRealPath on both sides with Path.startsWith rejects absolute, dot-dot and symlink escapes before readAllBytes; in-tree reports still read, missing files fail with the same NoSuchFileException as before.

R136.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) replaces uniqid and the attacker-controlled client_nonce prefix falls away with it; token format change is inherent to the fix and the dropped prefix is only implicit in the write-up.

R137.note: Positional ? parameter with the wildcards built into the bound value preserves the original LIKE semantics; the extra System/System.Data usings are unused but harmless.

R138.note: html.EscapeString on both interpolated fields is the right encoder for element content; the local variable named html shadows the package only after the RHS is evaluated, so it compiles and behaves as intended.

R139.note: Generic 'Invalid order ID' body keeps the 400 status and drops only the exception text; server-side logging is mentioned as advice but not added, which is not a regression.

R140.note: EJS <%= %> auto-escaping closes the XSS, but the write-up wrongly claims EJS ships with Express - it is a separate npm dependency, so without installing it every res.render fails at runtime; a one-line escape of closingNote would have been the minimal fix.

R141.note: Adds @csrf_protect below @router.post exactly as on the sibling route, which is the mechanism the middleware expects; no other change.

R142.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces the seeded System.Random and the response shape is unchanged; the now-ignored seed parameter and undisposed Create() instance are cosmetic.

R143.note: Build fails: $this->authorize() does not exist on a controller that extends nothing and lacks AuthorizesRequests; the can:refund,order middleware also denies everyone until the OrderPolicy the write-up only sketches in prose is actually created, which it does state as required.

R144.note: The cmd /C string sink is left in place and a character allowlist is the sole defence rather than exec.Command with separate argv for ping and nslookup, leaving leading-hyphen option injection open; the allowlist also rejects IPv6 literals and underscore hostnames the original accepted while the write-up claims legitimate targets are unaffected.

R145.note: A fixed name-to-module map is the right fix for import_module, but it hardcodes only two plugins (rejecting any other installed plugin with 400) and rewrites the module path to plugins.csv_export although the case docstring says plugins are top-level modules like csv_export, so even the listed plugins may fail to import.

R146.note: jwt.verify with a pinned algorithms list and try/catch to 401 closes the forged-token path; the new JWT_SECRET requirement, the 500 on missing config and the HS256 assumption are all stated openly.

R147.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) and executeQuery() replaces the concatenation; output and resource cleanup are unchanged.

R148.note: Removing [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] lets the globally registered AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute validate the POST; nothing else changes and the comment is updated to match.

R149.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter replaces the concatenated query; identical output and cleanup paths.
